title: Private backups: cross-region replication example + break-glass restore IAM role pattern
author: Bruno Silva
description: Context: Several Private design partners have asked for a concrete reference topology for DR storage that meets “regional outage” assumptions (and for a safer, auditable way to perform restores without granting long-lived admin creds). This PR adds an end-to-end example for cross-region replication of the Private backup bucket (S3) and introduces a “break-glass restore” IAM role pattern with least-privilege permissions and guardrails. Scope: examples only (no changes to existing modules’ defaults); the example composes the existing private backup bucket wiring from pr_318 and adds replication + restore role. What’s included: (1) New example `examples/private-backups-cross-region/` that provisions a primary backup bucket in `var.primary_region` and a replica bucket in `var.replica_region`, configures S3 replication with RTC disabled by default, and shows recommended lifecycle/retention settings aligned with the Day-2 ops toolkit. (2) KMS wiring guidance for replication: option A uses a Multi-Region KMS key for simpler ops; option B uses per-region keys and grants the replication role the necessary decrypt/encrypt permissions. (3) “Break-glass restore” role module in the example (pattern, not a reusable module yet): role is created disabled-by-default (no trust principals until explicitly set), includes short max session duration, requires MFA (when principal type supports it), and uses a permission boundary + explicit allowlist of S3 + KMS actions needed for restore-only workflows. (4) Documentation in the example README covering: required bucket/KMS settings, how to test replication, how to rotate principals for the break-glass role, and how to integrate with the `rw-private-dr restore plan/execute` flow. Notes/assumptions: This example assumes AWS (S3 replication). We intentionally avoided abstracting into a new module because we want field feedback from pilots first; once stable we can promote the pattern into `modules/private-backups` with toggles. Security note: The break-glass role is meant for time-bound restore assistance (customer operators + Redwood SE/SRE in a jointly controlled process). The trust policy examples include explicit placeholders for customer-controlled principals; Redwood should not be a default principal. Testing: `terraform fmt` + `terraform validate` + `tflint` against the example; manual apply in a sandbox account confirmed replication of a 10MB test object and successful assume-role with MFA requirements enforced. Follow-ups: add CloudTrail/CloudWatch alerting suggestions to the observability-pack docs and confirm the IAM boundary aligns with Security’s latest guidance on key handling.

review_conversation: Rafael Mendes (SRE): Can we make it obvious which IAM role actually performs S3 replication vs which role is used for restore? I don’t want operators to accidentally assume the replication role thinking it’s the break-glass role. Also, can we add a quick “replication health” check snippet to the README (list replication status/metrics)?

Bruno Silva (author): Good call. I split the naming: `rw-private-backup-replication-role` vs `rw-private-dr-breakglass-restore-role`, and added an explicit section in README: “Who assumes what?”. Also added a short replication verification snippet: `aws s3api head-object --bucket <replica> --key <...> --query ReplicationStatus` plus notes about replication lag and how to interpret `PENDING/COMPLETED/FAILED`.

Marcus Lin (Security): The trust policy defaults make me nervous. Please ensure the break-glass role cannot be assumed unless the operator sets `var.breakglass_trusted_principals` (empty by default), and add a Condition for ExternalId when cross-account is used. Also confirm we’re not granting kms:* anywhere (should be minimal).

Bruno Silva (author): Updated: trusted principals list is empty by default and the trust doc explicitly calls out enabling is a deliberate action. Added optional `var.breakglass_external_id` and wired it into the trust policy Condition when set. Verified the policy is only `kms:Decrypt`, `kms:Encrypt`, `kms:GenerateDataKey`, `kms:DescribeKey` scoped to the backup keys, plus `s3:GetObject*`, `s3:ListBucket`, and `s3:GetBucketVersioning` scoped to the relevant buckets/prefixes.

Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): Can we ensure the example pins provider aliases correctly for multi-region? I’ve seen “works locally” but fails in CI because the secondary region provider isn’t configured in `providers.tf` explicitly. Also please keep workflow changes minimal—do we need the workflow update?

Bruno Silva (author): Added explicit provider aliases (`aws.primary`, `aws.replica`) and wired them through each resource/module. For CI: I removed the workflow change (was only adding the new example path); instead updated the root README to document running `make validate-examples` locally. CI already discovers examples/ via the existing matrix.

Fatima Noor (Solutions / on-prem): For air-gapped customers using MinIO/NFS, this example won’t apply. Can we add a short note in the README that this is AWS-only and point to the staging-repo pattern used for on-prem? (Even just “see Day-2 ops docs”)

Bruno Silva (author): Added a “Non-AWS / on-prem” note at the top of the README: S3 replication is AWS-specific; for on-prem staging repositories use the Day-2 ops toolkit docs and the `rw-private-dr` offline bundle flow.
Marcus Lin (Security): One more ask—can we reduce `max_session_duration` on the break-glass role to 1 hour and add guidance that access must be ticketed and auditable (CloudTrail)?

Bruno Silva (author): Done. Set `max_session_duration = 3600` and added an “Audit/Evidence” section referencing CloudTrail events for `AssumeRole` + S3 object access and recommending change-ticket attachment (aligned with INT-932).
Rafael Mendes (SRE): Approved. This is enough to unblock DR game day planning; we’ll capture any gaps during the pilot drills.
Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): Approved after CI rerun.
release_notes: Added AWS example topology for cross-region replication of Private backup buckets.
Added a documented “break-glass restore” IAM role pattern with MFA/external-id guardrails and least-privilege S3/KMS permissions.
